richText: main is the Java entry point. SpringApplication.run starts the Spring application and returns its application context.
@SpringBootApplication supplies configuration for that startup. The annotation alone does not execute the application.

example.title: Start a Spring Boot application
description: Place DemoApplication in com.example.demo, above the packages containing application components.
explanation: SpringApplication.run creates the context and initializes the registered beans.
For a servlet web application with Spring Web, startup also starts the configured embedded server.

richText: @SpringBootConfiguration identifies the application’s configuration class. It is a specialized @Configuration.
@ComponentScan finds component classes in the application package and its subpackages by default.
@EnableAutoConfiguration allows Spring Boot to apply configuration when its conditions match.
You can use the underlying annotations separately. @SpringBootApplication is a convenient combination, not the only way to configure an application.
